title: Responsive header
summary: A stacked, centred header on phones that becomes one row on wider screens.
brief: Write it mobile-first. By default (phones): the brand, the links and the Sign up button stack vertically, centred, 12px apart. The links themselves sit in a centred row, 16px apart.
From 600px wide upwards: everything is one row, vertically centred. The brand is on the left, the button on the right, and the links sit between them with 24px between each link.
hints: Start with the phone layout as plain rules: .masthead as a column flex container, centred with align-items: center. .links is a row flex container.
Then add @media (min-width: 600px) { … } and, inside it, switch .masthead to a row.
In the media query: flex-direction: row and justify-content: space-between on .masthead, and gap: 24px on .links.
solutionNotes: The plain rules describe the phone: a centred column. The min-width media query only kicks in on wider screens and changes just what differs: the direction (which turns align-items: center into vertical centring, since the cross axis is now vertical) and the spacing. justify-content: space-between pushes the brand and button to the ends with the links in the middle. Mobile-first keeps the small-screen CSS simple and makes wider layouts additions rather than overrides.
